title: A stranger who stayed a lifetime
takeaway: A few minutes with the right person can change a whole life.
scene: The heading just says 'Three couplets'. The poet remembers someone he barely knew, who sat beside him for a short time and then left.

original: چند گھڑیاں اوکول سی بہہ کے دل نوں اگ لا گئے
میرے بے حس ستے دل وچ پیار دی شمع جلا گئے
transliteration: Chand ghariyaan o kol si beh ke dil nu agg la gaye
Mere be-hiss sutte dil vich pyaar di shamaa jala gaye
translation: They sat by me for a few moments and set my heart on fire.
In my numb, sleeping heart they lit the candle of love.
couplets.story: Someone sat beside him for just a few minutes. That was enough. His heart had felt numb, almost asleep, and suddenly it was burning like a lit candle.

original: نہ ای جان پچھان سی کوئی نہ سی سانجھ پنجالی
فیر وی عمر بھر دیاں یاداں میری جھولی پا گئے
transliteration: Na ee jaan pachhaan si koi, na si saanjh panjaali
Pher vi umar bhar diyaan yaadaan meri jholi pa gaye
translation: We weren't acquainted; we shared no bond at all.
Even so, they filled my lap with a lifetime of memories.
couplets.story: They were strangers. There was no history between them, nothing they shared. And still, that person left him with memories that will last the rest of his life.

original: جے ایہہ مہنگے موتی ہوندے شائد کوئی لے لیندا
بے مُلے اکھاں دے موتی گلے دا ہار بنا گئے
transliteration: Je eh mehnge moti honde shaayad koi le lenda
Be-mulle akhaan de moti gale da haar bana gaye
translation: If these were costly pearls, perhaps someone would have bought them.
But these worthless pearls from my eyes became a necklace around my neck.
couplets.story: His tears are like pearls. If they were real pearls, someone might at least want them. But tears are worth nothing to anybody else. So he wears them himself, like a necklace he can't take off.

deeper: Sufis describe moments when God's presence touches a sleeping heart without warning, briefly and unforgettably. A 'stranger' who wakes the heart in a few moments and leaves only longing behind fits that experience.
why: It captures how a short encounter can mean more than years with other people.
prompt: Has a short meeting or conversation ever stuck with you for years? Why?
notes: Couplet 2: 'saanjh panjaali' (a shared yoke) is a farming image for a bond between two people.
Couplet 3: printed 'انکھاں'; it is read as 'akhaan' (eyes), so the 'pearls' are tears.
